steps.title: The CA inventory
steps.body: Open Certification Authorities. Every certificate lives under the CA that issued it, so start from the issuer.

steps.title: Open the issuing CA
steps.body: Select the CA that issued the certificate to revoke. Revocation is recorded by the issuer: choosing the wrong CA means you will not find the certificate or its serial.

steps.title: Issued Certificates
steps.body: The Issued Certificates tab lists what the CA has signed. Here it holds 100 certificates, so scrolling is not practical.
steps.note: The CA's own certificate is also listed in this tab; do not confuse the two.

steps.title: Search by Common Name
steps.body: Filter by Common Name to find device-042 among the 100. Always confirm the serial number before acting on a match.

steps.title: Row actions
steps.body: The More actions menu of the matching row groups what you can do with that certificate, such as downloading its PEM or revoking it.

steps.title: Revoke Certificate
steps.body: Revoke when the key is compromised, the subject is no longer authorized or the identity must stop being accepted before it expires.
steps.note: Identify who uses this identity and prepare a replacement before revoking in production.

steps.title: Revocation reason
steps.body: Choose the reason that describes the incident. KeyCompromise fits because the device key is considered exposed.
steps.note: Only CertificateHold is reversible. Every other reason is final, and CertificateHold must not be used for a compromised key.

steps.title: Confirm the revocation
steps.body: Confirming changes the certificate status immediately in Lamassu.
steps.note: Status and publication are separate: validators see the change through OCSP or an updated CRL, which depends on its regeneration settings. Established sessions are not closed.

steps.title: Read the new status
steps.body: The row now shows REVOKED with the reason and the revocation time. Read the record again instead of trusting the dialog.
steps.note: Revocation does not delete the certificate or its key.
